purpose: Does SA-LHFiD hold up against established surrogate-assisted EAs on standard many-objective test problems, with and without observation noise, and does its deliverable 5-point set hold up? Fixed before any benchmark run (a timing pilot, one DTLZ2 noise-0.1 run per algorithm, was run and discarded; it only set the algorithm list below).
environment: .venv-saea (scripts/setup_saea_env.sh): ddmtolab 1.0.10 (MIT; Python port of PlatEMO algorithms), torch 2.5.1 CPU; one thread per worker
problems: DTLZ1, DTLZ2, DTLZ3, DTLZ4, DTLZ7 (src/diffusionnas/continuous.py; standard definitions, identical to PlatEMO/DDMTOLab)

main.note: the standard expensive-SAEA setting (D = 10, 300 evaluations, 11D - 1 Latin hypercube start), as used by K-RVEA, KTA2 and CSEA

noise: observed value = true value + N(0, (sigma x range_j)^2) on objectives 1..ceil(M/2), range_j = true-front nadir_j - ideal_j; sigma 0 (standard) or 0.1; noise seed shared by all algorithms for a given problem/M/sigma/seed
our_arm_details: src/diffusionnas/sa_continuous.py: Latin hypercube start; each round scale observations by observed min/max, fit DDMTOLab's Kriging (the model K-RVEA and KTA2 use) per objective, run the inner MOEA (population = reference vectors of continuous.reference_vectors(M): 105/120/126/156/275 for M = 3/4/6/8/10) for 30 generations from the best observed points, evaluate 20 novel candidates by spread pick; SBX eta_c 20, polynomial mutation eta_m 20 (5 for DTLZ1/3, as in the LHFiD paper)
baselines: k_rvea (Chugh et al. 2018), kta2 (Song et al. 2021), csea (Pan et al. 2019), parego (Knowles 2006): DDMTOLab 1.0.10 implementations with their default parameters, given n_initial and max_nfes; lhs: the whole budget as one Latin hypercube. Only the first `budget` logged evaluations are scored (KTA2 can overshoot by up to one batch).

indicators.primary: igd_plus: IGD+ of the nondominated noise-free values of all evaluated points to a dense true front, normalized by the true ideal and nadir
indicators.secondary: hv5_deliverable: greedy hypervolume subset selection of 5 points on the observed values, scored by their noise-free hypervolume (normalized, reference 1.1); hv5_oracle: the same selection on noise-free values

failures: a run exceeding 3 h wall clock (status timeout) or raising (status error) is recorded with its status; in the statistics it is ranked worst in its cell (counts against that algorithm); failure counts are reported per algorithm
statistics: per setting x problem x M x noise: Wilcoxon rank-sum (two-sided) of sa_lhfid against each other algorithm over 21 seeds, Holm over the 7 comparisons within the cell; report wins/ties/losses counts across cells per comparison; no claim from a single cell
claim_rule: SA-LHFiD is claimed competitive with an algorithm on a setting if, across that setting's cells, its Holm-significant losses on IGD+ are no more than its Holm-significant wins; claimed better if wins exceed losses and the median IGD+ ratio across cells is below 1. Noise-free and noisy cells reported separately.
expectation: stated in advance: K-RVEA and KTA2 are strong in the noise-free D=10 setting; ParEGO and MOEA/D-EGO degrade at M >= 6; the deliverable indicator is where noise matters
results_policy: results stay in artifacts/saea_benchmark (git-ignored) and chat; not written into report, papers or report page without the user's permission
excluded_before_running: moead_ego (Zhang et al. 2010): in the timing pilot it made 55 evaluations in 39 min at M = 4 and fewer at M = 6 (about 2.5 h or more per run), so it would exceed the run limit in most cells; it is also the baseline known to scale worst with M. Recorded here before any benchmark run.
